- **Time Complexity:** $O(n_{\text{max}})$ per path, where $n_{\text{max}}$ is the maximum bounce depth [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Source [S1] passages that 'Each recursive call corresponds to a single bounce of the light path' and that the algorithm uses a 'Maximum bounces n' as a hyper-parameter. It further notes that 'only a single forward and backward pass is needed from the DDF per bounce.' Since the computational cost per bounce is constant (one forward and one backward pass), the total time complexity for a path with maximum depth $n_{max}$ (referred to as $n$ in the text) is linear with respect to $n_{max}$, i.e., $O(n_{max})$.

- **DDF ($d, \xi$):** A scalar field $d(p, v)$ representing the distance to the surface along direction $v$ from $p$, and a binary field $\xi(p, v)$ indicating intersection ($\xi < 0.5$) [S1].

The evidence explicitly defines the DDF as consisting of a scalar field $d$ and a binary field $ξ$. It states that $d(p, v)$ is used to compute the next scene point $q = p + d(p, v)v$, which represents the distance to the surface along direction $v$ from $p$. It also states that $ξ(p, v)$ is checked against 0.5 to determine intersection (if $ξ < 0.5$, it returns environment light, implying no intersection with the scene geometry defined by $d$). Thus, $ξ$ indicates intersection status.
